We have sufficient raw material and component constituent parts of the HEPZATO KIT to meet anticipated demand and we intend to manage supply chain risk through stockpiled inventory and contracting with multiple suppliers for critical components.
We expect that the publication will support increased clinical adoption of and reimbursement for CHEMOSAT in Europe, and support reimbursement in various jurisdictions, including the United States.
We estimate that the total addressable market (“TAM”) for liver-dominant mCRC receiving third-line treatment is between 6,000 and 10,000 patients annually in the United States.
By targeting this patient population, we aim to provide a novel treatment option for those with limited therapeutic alternatives.
We expect approximately 90 patients will be enrolled in this randomized, controlled trial.
We estimate that approximately 7,000 patients annually in the United States are affected by HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer with liver metastases and are candidates for third-line treatment.
By focusing on this demographic, we intend to offer a novel therapeutic option to those patients with limited treatment alternatives.
We expect our research and development expenses to increase for the foreseeable future relating to the costs required to complete these Phase 2 clinical trials.
